triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix module asserted, as a source-backed output, that no personal-income-tax credit stage applies (sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies = false) and that the after-nonrefundable-credit, refundable-credit, and net-liability amounts are substantively zero, all grounded on a sales-and-use-tax guide sentence that establishes only the absence of a personal income tax before credits and says nothing about credits, credit ordering, or signed net liability.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us-sd/guidance/revenue/2026/sales-and-use-tax-guide/document-1, 47,544 chars): the phrase 'personal income tax' appears exactly once, in the 'Tax Basics' sentence used as the excerpt; the document contains no personal-income-tax credit, refundable-credit, or net-liability material, confirming the pre-fix branches had no basis in the cited source. Single-module commit; it also rewrites module.summary and upstream_source_check.rationale, adds a module.deferred_outputs block, and rewrites the companion test (sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies: false replaced by three '... _source_hold_applies: holds' expectations) plus the encoding manifest and .axiom/toolchain.toml. Numeric formulas for the three money outputs stay 0, so execution values do not change; what changes is the retracted Boolean output, the new typed Judgment holds (dtype Judgment, entity TaxUnit, effective_from 2026-01-01 / effective_to 2026-12-31, formula true), and the claim status of the zeros - a reviewer could argue this is hold/provenance discipline rather than a value correction, which is the main residual doubt. Note a self-inflicted slip inside this commit: the 'Fail-closed sentinel pending complete nonrefundable-credit authority' source label was attached to sd_pit_2026_resident_personal_income_tax_before_credits (the stage that IS source-backed) while sd_pit_2026_resident_personal_income_tax_after_nonrefundable_credits (a deferred output) kept the substantive label; the immediate follow-up commit 99c78e257 'Correct South Dakota source provenance' swaps those two labels back and also repoints us-sd/statute/10/43/2/block-1 to .../operative-text. Additional supporting prose added by this diff inside the module: "The pinned authority does not establish the absence of independently refundable credits or a complete signed net-liability surface." PR #1065 has no reviews or review comments; its body describes the post-fix state ('credit, refund, and terminal-liability zeros remain fail-closed sentinels behind typed holds').
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical and as not-a-defect and both fail: the diff retires the output `sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies` (dtype Boolean, formula false), replaces it with three `Judgment` source-hold rules whose formula is `true` with a new `effective_to: '2026-12-31'` window, and rewrites the companion test expectations from `sd_pit_2026_credit_stage_applies: false` to three `... _source_hold_applies: holds` entries — encoded meaning and output surface, not bookkeeping. The pre-fix encoding asserted, as source-backed outputs, that no credit stage applies and that the refundable-credit and signed net-liability amounts are zero, all proved by the single excerpt "South Dakota does not have a corporate, unitary, or personal income tax"; I read that provision through the pinned release (corpus_release us-rulespec-2026-08-03-ecps-pit-tariff-union) and the Sales and Use Tax Guide's only credit/refund language is sales-tax trade-in, returned-merchandise and credit-card-fee text, nothing about personal-income-tax credits, ordering, or signed net liability. So those values had no basis in the cited source and the fix removes/re-grounds them behind typed holds, which is exactly untraceable_branch; the author's own subject calls them "unsupported". The nearest alternative kind, wrong_entity_or_scope (the summary retracts "Complete ... pipeline" and the screen label says "scope/retire correction"), is a consequence of the ungrounded values rather than a mis-targeted entity or population, so it fits worse.

triage.verifier_notes: Caveats for the reviewer. (1) Strength is uneven across the three held stages: `after_nonrefundable_credits = 0` follows arithmetically from `before_credits = 0` (nonrefundable credits cannot go below zero), so that zero was defensible; the genuinely ungrounded ones are the refundable-credit zero and the signed net-liability zero, since a refundable credit can exist without an income tax. The defect is real but narrower than "all credit stages". (2) No computed Money value changes: all three Money outputs still have literal `formula: 0` and the formulas never reference the new hold rules — the fail-closed status lives only in `source:` strings, the new module-level `deferred_outputs` block, and the new Judgment outputs. A consumer reading only the numbers gets the same zeros; the meaning change is carried by the retired Boolean output, the three new `holds` outputs, and the test expectations. (3) This commit also introduced an off-by-one in the source relabeling: `sd_pit_2026_resident_personal_income_tax_before_credits` (the one output the authority does support) was labeled "Fail-closed sentinel pending complete nonrefundable-credit authority" while `..._after_nonrefundable_credits` kept "South Dakota Department of Revenue, no personal income tax"; the very next commit 99c78e257 swaps those two lines back. (4) Provenance: this is an intra-PR self-correction, not a fix to long-merged content — `git log --follow` on the module shows only efd821a3e (create), 551f1ac46f (this hold), 99c78e257 (provenance), all in PR #1065 merged 2026-07-24. If the corpus is meant to capture defects that survived into merged production rules, flag it on that ground rather than on kind.
